content.title: About
content.content: Cucumber salad with sour cream is a light dish made from fresh cucumbers sliced thinly and tossed with sour cream, seasoned with salt, pepper, and dill. The sour cream gives the salad a creamy, slightly tangy flavor while the cucumbers stay crisp.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: Cucumbers are about 95 % water, making the salad very refreshing.
Traditional Russian recipes use plain sour cream (20 % fat), but kefir or yogurt can be substituted.
Dill, a common herb in the dressing, has natural antibacterial properties.
The salad is a summer staple because it requires no cooking and cools the palate.
Sour cream helps absorb the fat‑soluble vitamins present in cucumbers.

items.title: Hydration
items.content: The high water content of cucumbers helps maintain the body’s fluid balance.

items.title: Low in calories
items.content: Cucumber salad is low‑calorie, making it suitable for weight‑management diets.

items.title: B‑vitamins
items.content: Cucumbers provide B5 and B6 vitamins, supporting metabolism.

items.title: Probiotic effect
items.content: Sour cream contains live cultures that can promote a healthy gut microbiome.

items.title: Minerals
items.content: The salad supplies potassium and magnesium, important for heart and muscle function.

items.title: Dairy allergy
items.content: Sour cream may trigger allergic reactions in people with lactose intolerance or milk protein allergy.

items.title: Salt content
items.content: Excessive salt in the dressing can raise blood pressure.

items.title: Bacterial spoilage
items.content: If sour cream is stored at improper temperatures, harmful bacteria can proliferate.

items.title: Foodborne illness
items.content: Cucumbers left at warm temperatures for too long may become a source of salmonella.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Serve the salad chilled as a snack or side dish with meat or fish. Garnish with extra dill, green onions, or toasted pumpkin seeds for added crunch.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Keep the prepared salad in an airtight container in the refrigerator for up to 2‑3 days. Stir before serving, as the sour cream may separate.
